title: A degree-two symmetric function on the symmetric group has a certificate of size at most n minus two
source_title: Uniqueness for 2-Intersecting Families of Permutations and Perfect Matchings

standard_prerequisites.name: Degree of a Boolean function on the symmetric group
standard_prerequisites.statement: The degree of f as a multilinear polynomial in the variables recording the images of the points.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the hypothesis bounded by two.

standard_prerequisites.name: Certificate size C(f)
standard_prerequisites.statement: The largest size of a common certificate over the members of the family, a certificate being a set of prescribed images.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the quantity bounded by n minus two.

standard_prerequisites.name: Influences and sensitivity
standard_prerequisites.statement: The degree bound restricts how the value of f can depend on the variables, so a function of high sensitivity cannot have degree two.
standard_prerequisites.use: It is the contradiction that closes the argument.

core_obligations: Assume the contrary, so that a degree-two function has a certificate of size exactly n minus one, and fix such a certificate (source line 269).

Build a Boolean function on four bits by evaluating f on products of four transpositions chosen according to the bits, and show it has degree at most two by substituting the corresponding value pattern into the polynomial of f (source lines 271-284).
Check the values of that four-bit function at the origin and at the four unit vectors, which gives sensitivity four (source lines 286-294).
Rule out a degree-two four-bit function of sensitivity four by inspecting the finitely many candidates, contradicting the degree bound (source lines 296-297).

proof_roadmap.step: Assume a certificate of size n minus one and fix it.
Transport f to a four-bit function and compute its degree.
Read off sensitivity four from the prescribed values.
Exclude all candidates by a finite check.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's labelled lemma at source lines 265-267: for n at least eight, a function on the symmetric group of degree at most two has a common certificate of size at most n minus two. The proof (source lines 268-297) is a contradiction argument that the statement hides entirely: from a supposed maximal certificate one builds a four-bit function by evaluating f on products of four transpositions chosen by the bits, the degree bound on f is transported through the substitution to show that this four-bit function still has degree at most two, its behaviour at the origin and at the four unit vectors shows sensitivity four, and a finite inspection of the candidates excludes every degree-two function of sensitivity four. The statement records only the size bound.
